title: FDA Complete Response Letters Citing Inadequate External or Historical Controls
summary: FDA complete response letters that rejected natural history, registry, or literature-based controls, with the deficiencies FDA cited and what it asked sponsors for.
body_markdown:
## FDA complete response letters that cited inadequate external or historical controls


FDA has repeatedly issued complete response letters (CRLs) for applications where efficacy depended on a comparison with a non-concurrent control, whether that was a natural history cohort, a disease registry, a literature-derived benchmark, or pooled historical trial data. A CRL is not a final rejection, and each of the four main examples below was later approved after the sponsor resubmitted. The Drugs@FDA action packages show that the objection is rarely "external controls are unacceptable." It is almost always that the specific comparator was not shown to be comparable, was not prespecified, measured outcomes differently, or lacked the patient-level data FDA needed to check the analysis.


The clearest examples are narsoplimab (BLA 761152), palovarotene/Sohonos (NDA 215559), telavancin/Vibativ for nosocomial pneumonia (NDA 022407) and the Nexium IV rebleeding supplement (NDA 021689/S-014). All four CRLs were later resolved: FDA approved narsoplimab in December 2025, Sohonos in August 2023, Vibativ for HABP/VABP in June 2013 and the Nexium IV supplement in March 2014[789](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=789)[792](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=792)[793](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=793)[794](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=794) . Two older actions from before the CRL format (Kytril and Synercid) and the Lumizyme post-CR registry analysis show the same reasoning.


### Summary of key actions


Product (application) CR / action date Type of non-concurrent control Core FDA objection What FDA said was needed Later outcome


Narsoplimab-wuug (BLA 761152) CRL October 15, 2021[525](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=525) Literature-based historical control; later a Japanese KSCTG registry Literature control could not reliably estimate the untreated response rate[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) ; the registry was not comparable to treated patients[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=23)[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=522) Confirmatory evidence; a well-matched historical control or an independently derived, prespecified threshold[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=103) ; individual patient data[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=28) Approved December 23, 2025 as YARTEMLEA, after a 2025 resubmission that added data, including expanded-access data[789](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=789)[790](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=790)


Sohonos, palovarotene (NDA 215559) CRL December 23, 2022[593](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=593)[605](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=605) Natural History Study (NHS) external control "Acceptability of the external control group" was a major unresolved issue, along with reliance on post-hoc analyses[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=24) Adequate support for efficacy[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=24) ; comparable assessment methods between trial and natural history cohort[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=467) Approved August 16, 2023, after a February 2023 resubmission and a June 2023 advisory committee[792](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=792)[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=477)


Vibativ, telavancin, HABP (NDA 022407) CRLs November 23, 2009[641](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=641) and December 21, 2010[654](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=654)[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=659) Historical patients given inadequate, inappropriate or delayed therapy Baseline characteristics "not comparable to those in the historical control groups"[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22) Two adequate and well-controlled HABP trials with specified design elements[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=504)[640](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=640) Approved June 21, 2013 for S. aureus HABP/VABP when alternatives are not suitable; FDA found the issues with the two registrational trials substantially resolved[793](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=793)[652](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=652)


Nexium IV (NDA 021689/S-014) CR November 26, 2008[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=539) Observational studies, literature reviews and a historical trial comparison Not adequate as primary evidence of efficacy[558](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=558)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=540) An additional adequate and well-controlled trial[544](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=544) Approved March 4, 2014, after a further action letter in June 2011 and a December 2012 resubmission[794](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=794)


### Narsoplimab (BLA 761152): literature control, then a registry control


**The 2021 CRL.** FDA concluded the original BLA failed to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness. The application rested on a 28-patient single-arm study plus a literature-based historical control used to justify the assumed untreated response rate[525](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=525) . FDA's review of that literature control identified:


- Unknown data validity and accuracy, endpoint measurement error, inconsistent response definitions and non-uniform definitions of 100-day survival across publications[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) .
- Limited confounder adjustment, non-standardized treatment-visit timing, convenience sampling and likely selection bias[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) .
- An assumed 15% untreated response rate supported only by the applicant's expert opinion[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) .
- No characterization of calcineurin inhibitor withdrawal or modification, a common part of TA-TMA management[528](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=528) .


FDA said the application lacked confirmatory evidence[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=103) . It described possible paths forward: a new randomized trial, or a single-arm trial with agreed responder criteria compared against a well-matched historical control and/or a prespecified threshold derived from an independent literature assessment. Alternatively, a resubmission could address the deficiencies with evidence of increased survival compared with an appropriate historical control[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=103) .


**The registry-based resubmission.** The sponsor then proposed the Japanese KSCTG transplant registry as an external control. FDA issued an Incomplete Response letter on April 28, 2025, rather than treating the resubmission as a complete response to the 2021 action[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=28) . FDA had advised that the KSCTG-based approach might not resolve the CRL deficiencies without individual patient data. It requested raw patient-level data, diagnostic algorithms and programming code to verify which registry patients met TA-TMA criteria. The applicant said the overall registry did not collect the data needed to verify or exclude a TA-TMA diagnosis[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=28) .


FDA's later review set out why the registry comparison was weak:


- **Temporal mismatch.** The registry covered 2000 to 2016 while treated patients enrolled from 2015 onward. This left a 3-to-7-year gap in which improvements in supportive care could favor narsoplimab[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=23) .
- **Geographic and practice differences.** The control was exclusively Japanese while the treated population was global[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=522)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) .
- **Different disease timing and selection.** Time from transplant to TA-TMA diagnosis was much earlier in registry controls[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=58) . Trial eligibility excluded early-onset, rapidly progressive and poor-prognosis patients, which produced a healthier treated population[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) .
- **Incomplete adjustment.** Key prognostic factors were left out of the propensity-score model, leaving residual confounding[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=527)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) . Poor propensity-score overlap meant some treated patients had no comparable controls[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=63)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) .
- **Missing registry variables.** The registry lacked high-risk TA-TMA factors and the components needed to determine response[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) .
- **Index-date imputation.** FDA considered it unlikely that the imputed "latent treatment day" for registry patients was missing completely at random[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=527) .


**The approval.** FDA approved narsoplimab-wuug (YARTEMLEA) on December 23, 2025 for adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older with TA-TMA[789](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=789) . The March 26, 2025 resubmission had added a response to the CRL deficiencies, external control data and compassionate-use expanded-access data, and the review team recommended approval "based on the data included with this resubmission"[790](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=790) . The approval review found substantial evidence of effectiveness in TMA-001 (17 of 28 patients responded), set against a historical response rate of 23.3% derived from 149 untreated patients in the published literature, with confirmatory evidence from expanded-access patients who had patient-level data[791](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=791) .


### Sohonos, palovarotene (NDA 215559): natural history external control


FDA's Complete Response letter was dated December 23, 2022[593](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=593)[605](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=605)[606](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=606) . It stated that the anticipated benefit of preventing new heterotopic ossification had not been established. It named two major unresolved issues: the "acceptability of the external control group (the Natural History Study, NHS) for evaluation of efficacy of the chronic/flare-up dosing regimen," and reliance on post-hoc analyses[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=24) .


Before the NDA, FDA had said the NHS might be acceptable as an external control but that data acceptability and comparability would be review issues. FDA also said randomized controls were preferred[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=467) . The review identified four groups of problems:


- **Comparability.** The treated and NHS populations differed on multiple demographic and disease measures[470](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=470) . The NHS-only group was older (19.9 vs. 14.1 years) and had higher baseline heterotopic ossification volume, more affected body regions and worse functional scores[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=247) .
- **Ascertainment.** Flare-ups were reported at 0.15 vs. 0.07 per subject-month in Study 301 vs. the NHS[466](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=466) . NHS contact was mainly every six months, compared with every three months (and every four weeks during flare-up dosing) in Study 301, and only Study 301 used daily symptom diaries[466](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=466) . Among 39 crossover patients, 0.6 flare-ups were recorded prospectively in the final NHS year, but patients retrospectively reported 1.1 for the same period when they enrolled in Study 301[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=465) .
- **Data collection.** Worsening of flare-ups was not systematically captured in the NHS[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=465) . CT scans were annual in the NHS vs. every six months in Study 301, and adverse events were not recorded in the NHS[468](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=468) .
- **Analysis.** The external-control analyses were post hoc, used non-validated measures and had unequal follow-up[470](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=470)[471](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=471) . The prespecified primary analyses in Study 301 and the Phase 2 program had failed[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=474) .


The CR page itself did not set out a detailed remedial study requirement beyond adequate support for efficacy[24](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=24) . Earlier FDA feedback had asked that every effort be made to use comparable assessment methods in the trial and the natural history control[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=467) . Ipsen resubmitted on February 16, 2023[475](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=475) . After a June 28, 2023 advisory committee, where most members found effectiveness despite the acknowledged limitations of the NHS control[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=477) , FDA approved Sohonos on August 16, 2023[465](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=465)[792](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=792) .


### Vibativ, telavancin (NDA 022407): historical controls in nosocomial pneumonia


FDA issued Complete Response letters for the nosocomial pneumonia/HABP indication on November 23, 2009[641](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=641) and December 21, 2010[654](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=654)[659](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=659) . A later February 2013 CR concerned manufacturing/CGMP, not the clinical deficiencies[649](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=649)[652](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=652) .


The sponsor compared telavancin-treated Phase 3 patients with historical patients who had received inadequate, inappropriate or delayed therapy. FDA concluded that "the baseline characteristics of the patients in the telavancin trials patients are not comparable to those in the historical control groups"[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22) . FDA said a comparability assessment would have to address age, APACHE-II score, percent ventilated, pathogens, adjunctive medications, ancillary care and management. It also said uncertainty about comparability justified discounting any noninferiority margin derived from the comparison[646](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=646)[656](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=656) . Other limitations FDA cited were differences in study design, prognostic factors, pathogen prevalence, mortality reporting periods and changes in standard of care over time[646](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=646)[656](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=656) . FDA rejected post-hoc selection of prognostic covariates as data-driven[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22)[646](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=646) . It also found pooling of Studies 0015 and 0019 problematic because of differing mortality risk factors[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22)[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=504) .


On historical evidence more broadly, FDA stated that published data supported noninferiority interpretation in NP/VAP only with all-cause mortality as the primary endpoint, not clinical response[651](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=651) . In those CR actions, FDA said it needed two adequate and well-controlled HABP trials[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=504) . These were to use radiographic and clinical entry criteria, independent chest-radiograph interpretation, uniform specimen-quality criteria, minimized adjunctive antibacterials and standardized renal follow-up[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=504)[640](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=640) .


FDA ultimately approved the HABP/VABP indication on June 21, 2013, limited to infections caused by susceptible Staphylococcus aureus when alternative treatments are not suitable[793](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=793) . After a November 2012 advisory committee majority recommended that limited approval, FDA found on review of the July 2012 resubmission that the clinical and statistical issues with the two registrational HABP/VABP trials were substantially resolved[652](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=652) .


### Nexium IV (NDA 021689/S-014): observational and literature comparisons


FDA issued a Complete Response on November 26, 2008[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=539) . The sponsor had supported a single adequate and well-controlled trial with observational studies and literature reviews. FDA said these were not adequate to serve as primary evidence of efficacy[558](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=558)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=540) . It cited lack of control and randomization, possible baseline differences and selection bias, ex-U.S. conduct and use of a comparator with unestablished efficacy[555](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=555) . The historical Lau omeprazole trial was a single-center Hong Kong study with a placebo rebleeding rate of 20%, compared with 10% in the Nexium pivotal study, and FDA found no clear explanation for the difference[551](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=551) . FDA required an additional adequate and well-controlled trial[544](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=544) . FDA approved the supplement on March 4, 2014 for risk reduction of rebleeding of gastric or duodenal ulcers following therapeutic endoscopy in adults. The approval letter records a further action letter on June 16, 2011 and a December 14, 2012 resubmission that responded to it[794](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=794) .


### Related actions showing the same reasoning


**Lumizyme, alglucosidase alfa (BLA 125291).** The February 27, 2009 CR cited CGMP, CMC, REMS and the lack of an agreed accelerated-approval verification study[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=456)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=38)[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=460) . It did not reject a historical control. After the CR, however, FDA invited Pompe Registry data matching infantile-onset patients to the Myozyme historical-control cohort as a possible route to regular approval[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=456) . FDA found that evidence limited for four reasons[162](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=162)[453](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=453)[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=169) :


- Only 25 of 48 patients were suitable for analysis.
- The comparator was non-concurrent.
- The registry mixed retrospective and prospective data, which could bias it toward survivors.
- There were no prospectively designed endpoints or statistical analysis plans.


Those limitations meant the data could not support approval for all ages[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=179) .


**Pre-CRL era actions.** Kytril (NDA 20-305/S-001) received a not-approvable letter on October 16, 1996. Comparisons with historical granisetron and prochlorperazine arms did not show that either regimen was effective. FDA asked for analyses against an appropriate historical control showing the regimens worked[788](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=788) . For Synercid's VREF bacteremia indication (approvable action, March 5, 1998)[765](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=765) , FDA found that published literature could not supply a reliable historical control. The reasons were differing regimens, infection definitions, endpoints and small sample sizes[759](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=759)[710](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=710) . FDA required a randomized, prospective confirmatory trial[763](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=763)[761](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=761) .


### Recurring deficiencies FDA identifies


Across these actions, FDA's objections fall into a consistent set of categories:


1. **Population non-comparability.** Baseline imbalances in age, disease severity, prognostic factors or geography (narsoplimab[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=23)[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=522) , Sohonos[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=247) , Vibativ[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22) ).
2. **Temporal drift in standard of care.** Registry or literature periods that predate the treated cohort (narsoplimab[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=23) , Vibativ[646](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=646) ).
3. **Unequal outcome ascertainment.** Different visit schedules, diaries, imaging frequency or endpoint definitions (Sohonos[466](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=466)[468](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=468) , narsoplimab literature control[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) ).
4. **Post-hoc or data-driven analyses.** Covariates or comparisons selected after unblinding (Sohonos[470](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=470) , Vibativ[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=22) ).
5. **Inadequate statistical adjustment.** Omitted prognostic covariates and poor propensity-score overlap (narsoplimab[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=527)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=63) ).
6. **Missing patient-level data.** Registry or published data that FDA cannot verify (narsoplimab[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=28)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=393) , Lumizyme[169](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=169) ).
7. **Unvalidated thresholds.** Assumed untreated response rates not grounded in independent evidence (narsoplimab[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=395) ).


FDA's statistical reviewers have framed a related concern using ICH E10. In the Nexium pediatric review (NDA 022101), FDA noted that a baseline-controlled study implicitly relies on an external control or efficacy threshold, so "the validity of the external control is crucial." It said the expected effect size should ideally be prespecified and justified[442](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=442)[438](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=438) . That review was not tied to a CRL. The action on that application was an approvable letter driven by cardiac safety[443](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=443) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


The remedies FDA asked for across these actions are consistent. In rare diseases FDA remains open to non-randomized designs where a well-matched historical control or an independently derived, prespecified threshold is agreed in advance[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=103) . It also expects comparable assessment methods between the trial and the control cohort[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=467) . It asks for individual patient data and code sufficient to verify eligibility and outcomes[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=28) . Where comparability cannot be shown, FDA has asked for a concurrent control: additional adequate and well-controlled trials[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=504)[544](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=544) or a randomized confirmatory trial[763](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-complete-response-letters-that-cited?showSourceNumber=763) .
